meaning:
συκο-μορέα (Rec. -μωραία, L, -μωρέα), -ας, ἡ, more commonly (so Aq., Sm., Psa.78:47, Isa.9:10) συκόμορος
(σῦκον + μόρον, the black mulberry),
a fig-mulberry, a sycamore: Luk.19:4 (cf. συκάμινος).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: He ran on ahead, and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was going to pass that way.
